label: UNBREAKABLE
voice_script: Berlin, 2009. At six-foot-five, Usain Bolt's frame was considered a disadvantage for a sprinter. The physics were against him. But his unique combination of stride length and raw power produced a top speed of nearly 28 miles per hour. That night, his main rival, Tyson Gay, ran a blistering 9.71—an American record. It still wasn't enough. For over a decade and a half, this record has seemed less like a milestone and more like a law of physics. Will it ever be broken?

screens.text: Most elite sprinters take 44+ steps to run 100 meters.

screens.clip_moment: Side angle view of Usain Bolt mid-stride, showcasing his long gait.

screens.text: The result: a world record of 9.58 seconds.
screens.clip_moment: The official clock on screen showing the final time of 9.58 seconds as Bolt crosses the finish line.

screens.text: His closest rival ran the 3rd fastest time in history... and wasn't even in the frame.
screens.clip_moment: Wide shot from behind the finish line, showing the significant gap between Usain Bolt and second-place Tyson Gay.

screens.text: No one has come within a TENTH of a second since.
screens.subtitle: The record has stood for 15+ years.

screens.text: The most unbreakable record in sport?
screens.clip_moment: Usain Bolt celebrating, looking iconic, doing his 'lightning bolt' pose.
